pages.name: Add or double
pages.text: Both columns start at 1. The left adds 2 each step: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The right multiplies by 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. That is [[exponential]] change, the same [[growth factor]] each equal step. The highlighted tops are the rises: 2 every time on the left, growing on the right, because each doubling adds as much as is there. So it starts behind, then passes at step 3.

pages.name: Guess step 10
pages.task: Keep both columns going to step 10. The left one will read `1 + 10 × 2 = 21`. Guess first: what will the doubling column read?
pages.why: Ten steps make ten doublings, so the right column reads 1 doubled 10 times, 1,024. Its last rise alone is 512, while the left column still rises by 2 a step.

pages.text: Each bar drops a dot onto the graph, its step along the bottom and its value up the side. The adding dots lie on a straight line, and the multiplying dots curve upwards. pages.name: One step on
pages.task: A bar is 48, and each step multiplies it by 1.5. What is the bar one step on?
pages.why: × 1.5 keeps the whole 48 and adds half of it, 24. So the next bar is `48 × 1.5 = 72`. The rise is a share of the bar, so a bigger bar would rise by more.

pages.name: 5% a year
pages.text: A percentage gives the factor. Growing 5% keeps the whole and adds 5%, so each year is × 1.05. Say a £1,000 pot grows 5% a year, beside one with £50 added each year. After 10 years it is `1,000 × 1.05¹⁰ ≈ £1,628.89` against £1,500, because each 5% is taken of a bigger amount. Run on, it doubles between years 14 and 15.

pages.why: You keep the whole pot, 1, and add 5%, 0.05, so each year is `× 1.05`. £1,000 becomes £1,050 after one year.

pages.name: Halving
pages.text: A factor below 1 shrinks the bar each step, which is called [[decay]]. Say a capacitor starts at 400 V and halves every 10 seconds, × 0.5 a step: 400, 200, 100, 50, 25. Halving `x` times is `(1/2)ˣ`, which is `2⁻ˣ`, since `b⁻ˣ = (1/b)ˣ` as in Powers and roots. The drops shrink too, because each is half of what is left. Half of a positive amount is still positive, so the rule gets ever closer to 0 V but never reaches it.

pages.name: Between the steps
pages.text: The rule works between the steps too. Half a step multiplies by `√b`, because two half steps must make one whole step, so `b^(1/2) = √b`, as in Powers and roots. At × 2 that is `√2 ≈ 1.414`, and `1.414 × 1.414 ≈ 2`. So the curve bends, rather than running straight from dot to dot, and like every `bˣ` it passes through (0, 1) and (1, `b`). This is why `b` must be positive: half a step at × −2 would need `√−2`, and no ordinary number times itself gives −2.

pages.name: Half a step
pages.task: A value of 100 grows × 9 each whole step, so it is 900 one step on. What is it half a step on?
pages.why: Half a step multiplies by `√9 = 3`, because two half steps, × 3 and then × 3, make the whole × 9. So 100 becomes 300 halfway, and 900 after the whole step.

pages.name: Which is exponential?
pages.task: Three rules, worked out at `x` = 1, 2, 3 and 4. Which one is exponential?
pages.why: Exponential means the same factor on each equal step, not fast growth: at `x` = 3, `x²` is ahead, 9 against 8, and at 4 they are level. Divide each value by the one before: `2ˣ` gives 2 every time. `x²` gives 4, 2.25, then 1.78, and `10x` adds 10 each step.

pages.name: 9% a day
pages.task: A count of 100 grows 9% a day. After a week it is about 183, close to the 163 that adding 9 a day gives. About how big is it after 30 days?
pages.why: Each day multiplies by 1.09, so after 30 days it is `100 × 1.09³⁰ ≈ 1,327`. A week in, it is close to adding, 183 against 163, but by day 30 it is far ahead, 1,327 against 370.

pages.name: Passing 30 V
pages.task: The capacitor starts at 400 V and halves every 10 seconds. When does it pass 30 V?
pages.why: `400 × 0.5ˣ`, with `x` counting 10-second steps, gives 50 V after 30 s and 25 V after 40 s. 30 V lies between, so it passes 30 V between 30 s and 40 s. Finding exactly when needs a way to undo a power, which comes in Logarithms (lesson 4) and Solving exponential equations (lesson 6).
